name: BigLake
oneLiner: Query and govern data in Cloud Storage and other lakes as BigQuery tables.
whatItIs: BigLake lets you treat files in Cloud Storage (and even S3 or ADLS) as governed BigQuery tables — without loading them. It's the piece that turns a plain object-store data lake into a 'lakehouse': you get BigQuery's SQL engine and fine-grained security (row/column-level access) over open formats like Parquet and Iceberg that live outside BigQuery's own storage. The point is one governance and access model across managed warehouse data and open lake data, so analysts and Spark jobs query the same tables under the same rules.

inPractice.narrative: A team keeps large open-format tables (Parquet/Iceberg) in Cloud Storage to stay portable and to share with Spark. They wrap those files in BigLake tables so BigQuery can query them in place, and apply row- and column-level policies centrally (often via Dataplex). Analysts run BigQuery SQL, Spark jobs read the same tables, and everyone is governed identically — no copy into the warehouse, no second set of permissions.

coreConcepts.detail: BigLake tables point at files (Parquet, ORC, Avro, Iceberg) in Cloud Storage or other clouds; BigQuery queries them without ingestion, so the data stays open and portable.
Row-level and column-level security and data masking apply to external lake data the same way they do to native BigQuery tables — the main thing plain external tables lack.
BigLake supports Apache Iceberg tables and a metastore so multiple engines (BigQuery, Spark, Trino) share one table definition and consistent reads.
Users query through the BigLake table without needing direct IAM access to the underlying bucket — access is delegated via a connection, centralising control.
BigLake (with BigQuery Omni) can query data sitting in S3 or ADLS, so one SQL surface spans clouds.
Dataplex manages catalog, policies and quality; BigLake enforces the access those policies define at query time.

whenToUse: Building a lakehouse: SQL + governance over open-format files in Cloud Storage.
Sharing one governed table between BigQuery and Spark/Trino.
Applying row/column-level security to lake data, not just warehouse data.
Keeping data in open formats (Iceberg) for portability while still querying with BigQuery.
Cross-cloud querying of data in S3/ADLS via BigQuery Omni.
whenNotToUse: Data already living happily inside native BigQuery storage with no external files — you don't need BigLake.
Simple one-off reads of a file where governance doesn't matter — a plain external table is simpler.
OLTP or low-latency serving — it's an analytical query layer.
Teams not on BigQuery at all — the value is BigQuery-centric governance.

keyFacts.label: Role
keyFacts.value: Governed query layer over lake files (a lakehouse enabler).

keyFacts.label: Engines
keyFacts.value: BigQuery plus Spark/Trino via a shared metastore.

keyFacts.label: Security
keyFacts.value: Row-level, column-level and masking over external data.

pricingShape: BigLake itself is mostly a capability layer — you pay for the BigQuery compute that runs the queries (on-demand per TB scanned or reserved slots), plus Cloud Storage for the underlying files, and any cross-cloud/Omni querying. There's no separate 'BigLake cluster'. So the cost profile mirrors BigQuery: partition and cluster your open-format tables, use columnar formats, and scan only what you need. Governance features come without a separate compute charge.
gotchas: It's a governance/query layer, not storage or a warehouse — people expect a product to 'run' and there's no cluster.
Query cost is BigQuery's, so unoptimised Parquet/Iceberg over huge data still scans (and bills) heavily.
Cross-cloud (Omni) has its own availability, egress and feature caveats versus native GCP querying.
Getting the delegation/connection IAM right matters — misconfiguration either blocks users or over-grants bucket access.
Iceberg/metastore setup adds moving parts versus a plain external table; only worth it when multiple engines or governance are in play.

equivalents.name: Amazon Athena
equivalents.note: Serverless SQL over S3; Lake Formation adds the governance BigLake bundles in.

equivalents.name: Synapse Serverless SQL
equivalents.note: On-demand SQL over ADLS files; Purview/Synapse handle governance separately.
